name: Castor oil on brows/lashes
lead: Applying castor oil to eyebrows and eyelashes is a folk remedy that practitioners say thickens or lengthens them. Castor oil is pressed from castor beans and consists mostly of triglycerides, with ricinoleic acid making up most of its fatty acids.[1]

Wikipedia's castor oil article lists laxative, skin-care and industrial uses and does not describe hair, brow or lash growth claims or evidence.[1] No clinical studies on the practice were identified.

paras: Castor oil is generally described as low in toxicity when topical, though Wikipedia notes the seeds contain ricin, which heating during extraction deactivates, and a bean allergen that is not present in the oil.[1] Ingestion can cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, castor oil is a common first suggestion for regrowing or thickening brows and lashes.

claims.claim: Castor oil regrows shaved or thinned brows
claims.believers: Forum users in an eyebrow-growth thread say it works and that shaved brows return in a few weeks, longer if tweezed; some users say they used it for about a month and saw lashes look healthier but not thicker.
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing castor oil for brow or lash growth. Shaved hair regrows on its own according to the normal hair cycle.

card.summary: Folk remedy of brushing castor oil on brows and lashes for thickness; popular online, untested in trials.
card.note: No trials identified; keep oil out of the eyes.

quick.overview:
Castor oil is a thick plant oil that many people brush onto brows and lashes hoping for thicker hair.

Forum users report both positive and underwhelming results.
quick.mechanism: Proponents attribute effects to ricinoleic acid and conditioning; no study has tested this for brows or lashes.
quick.risks: Topical use is generally described as low risk, but eye-area products can irritate.
